title: Quiet-window rituals and telemetry inkpad
body:
Context and intent:
This is a working sketch: a compact, operator-centered checklist + 7-day rollout calendar + draft release notes for features that prefer a quiet-window cadence (low-traffic windows with telemetry-centric stabilization rituals). The framing here is intentional: make release activity feel like a set of small rituals operators can run reliably, capture telemetry consistently, and escalate with minimal noise.

Audience:
- Release on-call / operator
- SREs monitoring latency/error regressions
- Product owners who need a lightweight release digest

High-level goals:
1) Avoid noisy mass rollouts during local peak hours by constraining high-risk flips to quiet windows.
2) Ensure telemetry samples are consistent and comparable across rollouts.
3) Make rollbacks fast and deterministic with a minimal human checklist.
4) Capture concise release notes that focus on operational impact and mitigations.

Operator rituals (pre-flight -> launch -> post-flight):
- Pre-flight (T-48 to T-1):
  - T-48: Tag the release in the release ledger and pin the rollout ticket (JIRA-RELEASE-3124). Add the quick-impact summary to the ticket top-level.
  - T-36: Smoke test locally using the trimmed dataset (local-smoke/fast.json). Run the release-specific unit of the stability harness (tools/stability-harness --short).
  - T-24: Schedule quiet-window slot in the team calendar (default: 02:00–04:00 UTC). Notify stakeholders via #release-ops: short message + link to ticket.
  - T-8: Confirm observability sampling rates: ensure the new release has the same telemetry sampling as baseline (trace-sample=1.0 for first 30m if flagged). Increase token-level logging retention to 6h for the window only.
  - T-2: Prepare canary cohort list (a small percentage by user cohort, plus internal alpha cohort). Document cohort IDs in the ticket.
  - T-1: Day-of checklist: backup config snapshots, export KV cache metrics baseline, and verify rollback playbook is pinned and accessible.

- Launch (quiet-window):
  - 00:00: Toggle canary cohort to release variant A (5% traffic) using the traffic-router UI. 
  - +02m: Verify the canary warped requests (sampled traces) are arriving. Check the ingress to model mapping.
  - +10m: Run the smoke-throughput probe (5 concurrent sessions, kept under latency SLO). If any p99 > baseline + 30%, STOP and roll back to previous commit.
  - +30m: If canary passes, increase to 25% and continue. If any new error class appears (non-200, model-timeout), escalate to on-call and pause further ramp.
  - +60m: If stable at 25%, and business has greenlight, schedule gradual ramp to 100% across next quiet-window depending on capacity.

- Post-flight (first 24h):
  - Hourly for first 6h: quick health check ping (latency, error-rate, saturation). Log a one-line status update to ticket.
  - Post-6h: Add a short telemetry digest to the ticket: token cost delta, p50/p95/p99 deltas, error-rate deltas by endpoint.
  - 24h: Formalize stabilization: snapshot traces for the first and last hour, move to t+24h retrospective notes.

Minimal checklist (can be printed as card for operator):
- [ ] Release tag & ticket updated
- [ ] Quiet-window slot scheduled and stakeholders notified
- [ ] Local smoke pass completed
- [ ] Observability sampling confirmed (traces/metrics/events)
- [ ] Canary cohort defined and documented
- [ ] Rollback commit and config snapshot validated
- [ ] Post-launch hourly pings enabled

7-day rollout calendar (example for a 2-phase rollout):
- Day 0 (Tue): pre-flight checks complete, alpha cohort smoke runs, docs updated.
- Day 1 (Wed quiet-window 02:00–04:00 UTC): roll canary -> 5% for 60m, monitor.
- Day 2 (Thu quiet-window): ramp to 25% for 60m if no alerts.
- Day 3 (Fri): operational buffer day (no ramp), collect telemetry digest and QA review.
- Day 4 (Mon quiet-window): ramp to 50% if stable; open payment or billing-sensitive endpoints last.
- Day 5 (Tue): optional hold/review day; patch if needed.
- Day 6 (Wed quiet-window): finalize ramp to 100% or plan phased continued ramp into Dedicated capacity.

Release notes (draft):
Title: lightweight routing + cache warming (release-3124)
Summary: This release introduces targeted routing heuristics to reduce cold-start impact for medium-seq workloads and a conservative cache-warming path to populate prefix caches for common prompt shapes. Expected net effect: modest latency improvement for 90% of requests, slight token-cost increase (+0.6% observed in alpha).
Operational impact:
- New config flags: routing.optimistic_locality (default off) and cache.warm.enabled (default on for internal cohorts).
- Observability: added a new metric routing.cohort.locality_hit_rate and an event tag release=3124.
- Rollback: revert to commit abcd1234 (rollback script included in ticket).
Known issues:
- Rarely (observed in 2/1,000 alpha samples) requests to the reranker path saw transient p99 increases when warm-up concurrency aligned with heavy background batching. Watch for p99 regressions in /rerank endpoint.

Telemetry sampling plan (how we capture comparable signals):
- Keep trace sample=1.0 for first 30m of each ramp step.
- Capture 100% of error traces for 24h post-deploy.
- Export token-level accounting to the release ticket hourly for first 8h.

Quick escalation flow (if any gate trips):
1) Operator pauses ramp and sets traffic back to last stable cohort.
2) Call SRE on-call and attach the latest exported traces.
3) If rollback threshold met (p99 > baseline + 50% for 30m OR error-rate > baseline * 3 for 15m), run the rollback script and declare incident.

Notes-to-self and open questions (sticky):
- Should we automate the T-8 sampling check in the router? (Rowan: follow-up with router team)
- Consider a one-click snapshot of KV-cache state at T-2 (useful for postmortem comparisons).
- Is the alpha cohort size too small? 5% may not surface edge-cohort regressions; but pushing higher increases blast radius. Tradeoff needs product decision.
- Add a short cheat-sheet for on-call to interpret routing.cohort.locality_hit_rate (Lena to draft).

Next steps (short runbook items):
- Ethan: add the one-line health check script to the ticket (ops/health-check.sh) and test it against staging.
- Maya: align quiet-window scheduling automation with on-call calendar and add RSVP semantics to #release-ops.
- Rowan: prototype router preflight that validates sampling rates programmatically.

Appendix (operator quick commands):
- Check canary state: ./ops/traffic-router status --release=3124
- Pause ramp: ./ops/traffic-router pause --cohort=canary --release=3124
- Rollback: ./ops/rollbacks/roll-back-to abcd1234 --release=3124 --reason="auto-threshold"

This doc is intentionally compact. Use it as the basis for a more formal runbook if the pattern proves repeatable across three releases. For now: keep it lean, encourage operators to leave a one-line note after each quiet-window run ("Clear/Investigate/Rollback"), and we can iterate on templating and automation later.

Raw notes (scratchpad, chronological):
- 2026-09-14 14:02 Ethan: initial sketch during on-call handover
- 2026-09-15 09:10 Maya: confirmed tool names and added ops scripts
- 2026-09-18 16:22 Rowan: suggested programmatic sampling validation (TO DO)
- 2026-09-20 11:45 Lena: will draft the locality_hit_rate interpretation cheatsheet

End of doc.
